title.narrative: PIMS–10100 Development of the Second Biennial Transparency Report and the combined Third Biennial Transparency and Sixth National Communication Report of Morocco under the UNFCCC

description.narrative: The preparation of the project document for Morocco represents a critical step toward strengthening the national framework for transparency and climate reporting under the Paris Agreement. This project responds to Morocco’s commitment to enhance the quality and consistency of its climate data and to institutionalize mechanisms for regular reporting. Through the development of the Second Biennial Transparency Report (BTR2), and the Third Biennial Transparency Report (BTR3) combined with the Sixth National Communication (NC6), the project will consolidate lessons learned from previous reports and integrate new methodologies aligned with the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF). The expected results include a comprehensive and high-quality national greenhouse gas inventory, improved systems for monitoring and evaluating mitigation and adaptation actions, and strengthened institutional coordination among key ministries and stakeholders. The project will also foster the integration of climate information into national planning processes and support the development of long-term strategies for low-emission and climate-resilient development. Ultimately, the project document sets the foundation for building a sustainable national transparency system that enhances Morocco’s capacity to meet its international commitments while supporting evidence-based climate policy and sustainable development goals.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
